text: Databases are organized systems for storing and managing information. Traditional databases use tables to keep data in rows and columns, similar to a spreadsheet. To get information from them, you write queries, which are instructions that ask specific questions. SQL databases follow a fixed structure, while NoSQL databases are more flexible and can handle different data types. Data modeling helps you plan how information connects before you build anything. Indexes work like a book's index, making searches much faster. Choosing the right database depends on your needs, so understanding these basics helps you make better decisions.
